name: Caro-Kann Defence
summary: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5: Black prepares ...d5 with a pawn so the centre is challenged without shutting in the light-squared bishop. A solid structure, good endgames, and a clear plan against each White system.

black: Challenge e4 with ...d5 at move two; after ...dxe4 develop the c8 bishop to f5 or g4 before ...e6.
Keep the structure solid: pawns on c6 and e6 guard d5 and the king.
Against the Advance, hit the chain at its base with ...c5 and develop ...Nc6 and ...Ne7.
Against the Panov, blockade the isolated d-pawn on d5 and trade pieces.
white: Use the extra space: h4 and h5 against the bishop on g6 in the Classical.
In the Advance, keep the e5 pawn and gain kingside space.
In the Panov, play with the isolated d-pawn: active pieces and a kingside attack.

structures.name: Classical: c6 and e6 against d4
structures.text: White has a pawn on d4, Black none in the centre, but the pawns on c6 and e6 control d5 and are very hard to break. White often castles long and pushes h4 and h5; Black castles on either side once the bishop is safe.

structures.name: Advance: e5 and d4 against e6, d5, c6
structures.text: A closed chain, but Black's light-squared bishop is outside it on f5. Black hits d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6; White uses the space on the kingside.

structures.name: Panov: the isolated d-pawn
structures.text: After c4 and exchanges White has an isolated pawn on d4. Black blockades on d5 with a knight, trades pieces, and attacks the pawn in the endgame.

black: Light-squared bishop: f5 or g4, outside the pawn chain. It is the reason for 1...c6.
d7 knight: makes ...Ngf6 safe and supports the ...c5 and ...e5 breaks.
f6 knight: defends h7 and the kingside.
Queen: c7 in the Classical, b6 against the Advance's d4 and b2.
white: g3 knight: chases the f5 bishop with tempo.
h-pawn: h4 and h5 gain space and take g6 from the bishop.
e5 pawn in the Advance: the spearhead of the space advantage.

lines.name: Classical, 4...Bf5: the bishop goes first
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5 5. Ng3 Bg6 6. h4 h6 7. Nf3 Nd7 8. h5 Bh7 9. Bd3 Bxd3 10. Qxd3 e6 11. Bd2 Ngf6 12. O-O-O Be7

notes.1...c6: Prepares ...d5 with a pawn behind it.
notes.3...dxe4: Black gives up the centre pawn for free development.
notes.4...Bf5: The bishop leaves before ...e6 shuts it in.
notes.6.h4: Threatens h5 to trap the bishop.
notes.6...h6: Gives the bishop the h7 square.
notes.8.h5: Gains space; the bishop must go to h7.
notes.9.Bd3: Offers to trade Black's best bishop.
notes.10...e6: Now ...e6 costs nothing: the bishop is already traded.
notes.12...Be7: Black develops and castles short; the h5 pawn can become a target later.

lines.name: Advance, Short Variation: hit the chain with ...c5
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. e5 Bf5 4. Nf3 e6 5. Be2 c5 6. Be3 Nd7 7. O-O Ne7 8. c4 dxc4

notes.3.e5: Gains space and closes the centre.
notes.5...c5: Attacks the base of the chain at d4. Two moves with the c-pawn are fine in a closed position.
notes.7...Ne7: Heads for c6 or f5, where it hits d4.
notes.8.c4: White opens the centre while Black's king is still on e8.
notes.8...dxc4: Black takes and frees the d5 square for a knight.

lines.name: Exchange Variation: symmetrical but not dead
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. Bd3 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Bf4 Bg4 7. Qb3 Qd7 8. Nd2 e6 9. Ngf3 Bxf3 10. Nxf3 Bd6

notes.3.exd5: Symmetrical pawns; White plays for a small edge with active pieces.
notes.6...Bg4: Develops outside the pawn chain with an attack on the queen.
notes.7...Qd7: Defends b7 along the seventh rank and keeps the queen active.
notes.8...e6: Solid: d5 is guarded and the f8 bishop is free.
notes.9...Bxf3: Trades the bishop so White has fewer pieces fighting for e5.
notes.10...Bd6: Offers to trade White's active f4 bishop.

lines.name: Panov Attack: blockade the isolated pawn
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. c4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e6 6. Nf3 Be7 7. cxd5 Nxd5 8. Bd3 Nc6 9. O-O O-O

notes.4.c4: The Panov: White hits d5 and accepts an isolated d-pawn for active play.
notes.5...e6: Solid: the f8 bishop develops and d5 stays guarded.
notes.7...Nxd5: The knight sits in front of the isolated pawn: the ideal blockading square.
notes.9...O-O: Black is ready to trade pieces and aim at d4.

lines.name: Two Knights: trade on f3 and play ...e6
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Nf3 Bg4 4. h3 Bxf3 5. Qxf3 e6 6. d4 Nf6 7. Bd3 dxe4 8. Nxe4 Qxd4

notes.3...Bg4: Pins the knight, planning to trade it.
notes.4...Bxf3: Trade now: Black gives the bishop pair for a sound structure.
notes.5...e6: Pawns on c6, d5, e6: light squares, so the f8 bishop stays free.
notes.8...Qxd4: Black takes the pawn White left; White has the bishop pair and quick development in return.

traps.name: 5.Qe2: the smothered mate on d6
traps.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Qe2 Ngf6 6. Nd6#

notes.4...Nd7: Prepares ...Ngf6 so that White cannot double Black's pawns with Nxf6+.
notes.5.Qe2: A sneaky queen move: it sets up a pin on the e-file.
notes.5...Ngf6: The mistake: natural, but the e7 pawn is now pinned.

traps.punishment: 6.Nd6 is mate: the e7 pawn cannot take because the queen on e2 pins it to the king, and Black's own pieces block every escape square. After 5.Qe2 play 5...Ndf6, keeping the e-file closed.

traps.name: 7...h6?: the knight sacrifice on f7
traps.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Bc4 Ngf6 6. Ng5 e6 7. Qe2 h6 8. Nxf7 Kxf7 9. Qxe6+ Kg6

notes.6.Ng5: Aims at f7 and e6 together with the c4 bishop.
notes.7...h6: The mistake: it chases the knight, but the knight does not retreat.

traps.punishment: 8.Nxf7 Kxf7 9.Qxe6+ Kg6 and 10.Bd3+ Kh5 11.Qh3 is mate. The e6 pawn was guarded only by f7, and the queen and the c4 bishop aim straight at it. Play 7...Nb6 first to chase the bishop off the diagonal.
